clue.text: Treated as canards — her prophecies were

definitions.text: Treated as canards — her prophecies were

indicators.note: treated in the sense of processed or worked on, so the letters of the next two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman whose predictions were all dismissed as false rumours.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: 'Treated' rearranges AS CANARDS, and a canard is a baseless rumour, which is how her true prophecies were received.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Trojan princess was cursed to prophesy truly but never be believed.

clue.text: Choose randomly from play's actors, a great many

parts.note: the actors in a play make up its cast
lots means a great many

explanation.surface: Picking a big crowd of performers from a drama's company.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: drawing lots is deciding a choice by chance.

clue.text: Prosecute girl

definitions.meaning: to take legal action against someone
a girl's name, short for Susan

explanation.surface: Taking a young woman to court.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym for bringing a lawsuit, and also a common female first name.

clue.text: Runs in a boy for fire-raising

indicators.note: in says the runs abbreviation goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: a boy is a son
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A lad racing about, apparently on a fire-starting spree.
explanation.definitionFit: Fire-raising is the British legal term for deliberately setting fire to property.

clue.text: Vermouth's not to be referred to, not at all

parts.note: a thing not to be referred to is one you must not mention
IT is Italian vermouth, as in gin and it; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A drink so shameful nobody should mention it.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as 'IT is not to be referred to', i.e. an instruction never to mention IT. IT for Italian vermouth is a dated British bar usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are polite replies to thanks, waving away any need for gratitude.

clue.text: Trainee jumping racecourse

indicators.note: jumping suggests letters leaping about into a new order

explanation.surface: A novice rider taking fences at a horse-racing track.
explanation.walkthrough: AINTREE, near Liverpool, is the British course that hosts the Grand National steeplechase.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a famous English venue for horse racing over jumps.

clue.text: Price cut for lettuce

indicators.note: cut means the last letter is chopped off the word for price

parts.note: the price of something is its cost

explanation.surface: A discount on salad leaves at the greengrocer.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: cos is the long-leaved variety also called romaine.

clue.text: Lobby Tory over hunt

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, the Tory party
to course is to hunt game with hounds by sight

explanation.surface: A Conservative MP pushing a political agenda about fox hunting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lobby' looks like a verb about campaigning, but it is the noun for an entrance hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a large open hall in a station or building where people gather.

clue.text: Extremely stark, the old Hebridean island

indicators.note: extremely points to the extreme letters, the first and last, of the next word

parts.note: ye is an old form of the

explanation.surface: A bleak, old-fashioned description of a Scottish isle.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the largest island of the Inner Hebrides, off Scotland's west coast.

clue.text: Running tests on hat

indicators.note: running means the letters are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: Carrying out trials on a piece of headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the wide-brimmed cowboy hat named after its maker.

clue.text: Girl in French city

definitions.meaning: a city in Lorraine, north-east France

explanation.surface: A young woman travelling in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A common girl's name, and also the city in eastern France.

clue.text: Bloomer at university, interrupting endless row

indicators.note: interrupting means one piece breaks into the middle of the other
endless means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a row is a line
UP means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A student's embarrassing gaffe disrupting a shouting match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder, but here it means a flowering plant. 'endless' turns LINE into LIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword sense: a bloomer is something that blooms, and the lupin is a garden flower.

clue.text: Penny had a meal on board river vessel

indicators.note: on board puts the eating inside the river, as passengers are inside a ship

parts.note: taken as the word river
ate means had a meal

explanation.surface: A woman named Penny dining on a riverboat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' looks like a diner's name, but it is the coin; 'vessel' is a ship, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A privately owned armed ship licensed to attack enemy shipping is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Colour of biscuit — about to disappear!

indicators.note: to disappear means the letters for about vanish from the biscuit

parts.note: a macaroon is an almond biscuit
CA, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A cookie's shade that is fading away.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a dark brownish-red shade.

clue.text: Dark lady, Ms Davis, about to direct

indicators.note: about means the first name goes around the other piece

parts.note: Bette Davis was the Hollywood film star
to run something is to direct it

explanation.surface: Bette Davis, sultry star, poised to direct a film.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman with dark brown hair is described this way.

clue.text: Method of solving a problem in heart of Africa — a land in panic

indicators.note: in places the middle pieces inside the word for panic

parts.note: terror is extreme panic

indicators.note: heart of picks out the central letters of the continent's name

explanation.surface: A puzzling dilemma amid a frightened central African country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart of' takes RI, the middle two letters of AFRICA; RI, A and LAND go into TERROR.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: trying options repeatedly until one works is a basic way to tackle a puzzle.

clue.text: Student beginning in little job that pays

indicators.note: beginning in points to the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: a nice little earner is British slang for a lucrative job

explanation.surface: A trainee starting out in a modest paid position.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone still acquiring a skill, as in a learner driver.

clue.text: Expedition heading for Sumatra, a distant island

indicators.note: heading for takes the head, the first letter, of the next word

parts.note: far means distant
I is the map abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A trip to a remote Indonesian island.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is an organised journey, especially to see wildlife in Africa.

clue.text: Groom about to be put in prison

indicators.note: to be put in means the word for about goes inside the prison

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure, slang for a prison (short for penitentiary)
RE means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A bridegroom about to be locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' looks like the man at a wedding, but it is a verb: to tidy oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym verb: to smarten one's appearance, as a bird tidies its feathers.

clue.text: Bother over sauce

parts.note: to pester is to bother, so a pest is a bother
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Annoyance at having to make a pasta topping again.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the Italian basil and pine-nut sauce.

clue.text: Monster seen in bog, recently

indicators.note: seen in says the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A creature spotted lately in a swamp.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant of fairy tales, a kind of monster.

clue.text: Pick up some jungle animals

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Catching a few creatures in the rainforest.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to gather bit by bit, as gleaners collect leftover grain.

clue.text: There's nothing to get worked up about on waste ground

definitions.text: There's nothing to get worked up about

indicators.note: ground as in ground down or crushed, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Reassurance that a patch of derelict land is nothing to fret over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like part of 'waste ground', but it is the anagram signal on ON WASTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal idiom: the phrase means no trouble, nothing to stress over.

clue.text: Greek character having high tea

indicators.note: high in the sense of intoxicated, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A Greek person enjoying an evening meal of high tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high tea' reads as a British early-evening meal, but 'high' is the anagram signal on TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: English bishop's sin

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the title given to a bishop

explanation.surface: An Anglican bishop's wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym verb: to go astray morally, to do wrong.

clue.text: Limit beer in grounds

parts.note: to ration is to limit supply
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Restricting drinking at a sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grounds' suggests sports fields, but it means reasons.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the underlying reasons or justification for a decision.
